title: Install standup: firewall + NFS debugging (Oct 2024)
body:
Weekly install standup notes — focus: recurring customer NFS mounts failing under burst load + intermittent control-plane timeouts behind customer firewall; session log compiled Oct 11–13, 2024.

Attendees: Avery Chen (owner), Miguel Reyes, Priya Nair, Jordan Blake, Lina Park, customer engineering rep (ACME Cloud Ops).

Summary / high-level:
- Customer ACME reported repeated pod-level timeouts when kubelet tries to mount NFS volumes after a scale-up event. Problem only reproduces when customer firewall has deep packet inspection (DPI) + stateful connection tracking enabled; when firewall in passthrough mode mounts succeed.
- Separately, occasional control-plane RPCs from our private control plane to the on-prem installer node were dropped for ~30s during peak traffic windows. Suspected MTU fragmentation + AWS Direct Connect peer path asymmetry.
- This week we did three live repro attempts with customer, captured tcpdump and kernel logs; root cause appears to be twofold: (1) NFS write bursts create many short-lived ephemeral TCP sessions that interact poorly with the customer's firewall connection tracking table size (nf_conntrack aging), and (2) small MTU on the customer uplink (~1400) plus an overlay (VXLAN) causing fragmented packets that some firewall boxes drop if DF bit logic triggers.

Notes from debugging sessions:
1) Repro steps and artifacts:
   - Repro scenario: scale deployment from 10 -> 60 replicas, each mounts NFS PV and writes 256KiB files in a tight loop for 30s. Observed ~45% of mounts fail with EIO or timeouts.
   - Captured artifacts: tcpdump (see linked Slack thread for pcap), dmesg from node-3 during repro, nf_conntrack counters snapshot before/after.
   - Observed high number of SYN_RECV / TIME_WAIT entries. conntrack table exceeded soft limit and started evicting entries, which led to connection resets mid-handshake.

2) Firewall and conntrack specifics: Miguel found the customer's Palo Alto appliances have conntrack-like simultaneous-flow thresholds set aggressively (default 65k). Under the repro we hit ~72k tracked flows and the appliance enters a protective mode that silently drops new flows for ~20–40s. This matches the control-plane RPC drop windows.

3) MTU and fragmentation: Priya validated that VXLAN (overlay) + physical MTU 1400 leads to inner-packet sizes > outer MTU, creating fragments. Some DPI rules on customer's firewall discard fragments or fail reassembly when DF bit set. We saw mismatched MSS clamping (no clamp at edge), so TCP sessions tried to send 1460 bytes and fragmentation occurred.

Triage decisions made in-standup:
- Short-term mitigation for customer: enable client-side mounting option 'nconnect=4' and lower per-write buffer to 64KiB to reduce simultaneous short-lived connections. Also suggest enabling conntrack timeout tuning on firewall (increase table size or reduce timeout aggression). (Action: Miguel to coordinate with ACME ops — JIRA PD-4123).
- Network workaround: set MTU on worker network interface to 1300 and enable MSS clamping on node egress rules to avoid fragmentation through overlay. (Action: Priya to prototype a node-init script; PR referenced in linked_artifacts).
- Control-plane fallback: add an extra retry/backoff at installer RPC layer for idempotent calls to withstand 30–60s connection chaos. (Action: Jordan to open small patch to retry logic — JIRA PD-4178).

Open blockers and risks: 
- Customer cannot temporarily increase conntrack table on their firewall without an enterprise change request; timeline uncertain (could be days). That increases risk of recurring outages during scale events.
- Lowering MTU to 1300 may slightly reduce throughput and increase CPU on nodes due to additional fragmentation/overhead — need to quantify cost.
- The proposed client-side NFS tweaks reduce throughput but are acceptable as short-term band-aid; longer-term we want fewer ephemeral TCP sessions.

Action items (owners + due dates):
- Miguel Reyes: Coordinate with ACME Cloud Ops to request conntrack policy change or apply temporary exception. Update JIRA PD-4123 with firewall vendor ticket id. Due: 2024-10-15.
- Priya Nair: Create node-init script to set MTU 1300 + MSS clamp (iptables --clamp-mss-to-pmtu) and iterate on an image; open PR for deploy-scripts. Link PR in PD-4178. Due: 2024-10-16.
- Jordan Blake: Implement conservative retry/backoff for control-plane RPCs (idempotent) and add observability for dropped RPCs. Add unit tests. PR -> deploy-control-plane. Due: 2024-10-18.
- Lina Park: Draft temporary install-playbook section titled 'Customer with strict DPI/firewall' with steps and repro checklist; include tcpdump capture checklist. Due: 2024-10-14.
- Avery Chen: Run cost/latency microbenchmarks after MTU change on staging cluster to quantify impact; publish numbers in the Confluence page. Due: 2024-10-17.

Customer communication notes:
- Draft message approved in-standup: explain technical cause (conntrack + MTU) and short-term mitigations (nconnect, lower write size, node MTU change). Avoid vendor specifics; offer to pair with their network team for a vendor ticket. (Owner: Miguel).
- Escalation path: if firewall vendor change not approved by 2024-10-16, prepare to schedule controlled maintenance window to apply MTU/MSS changes and test. (Owner: Avery).

Runbook / docs next steps:
- Add a section to the Onprem Install Checklist (Confluence) covering 'NFS at scale — firewall conntrack considerations' with recommended default limits and example iptables rules. (Owner: Lina).
- Add a small troubleshooting script to collect: conntrack counters, iptables/nft rules, dmesg, ifconfig mtu entries, and recent tc events; attach to the new playbook section. (Owner: Priya).

Observability / telemetry adjustments:
- Add Prometheus alert for nft_conntrack_count high on installer nodes (threshold = 70% of soft limit). (Owner: Jordan).
- Add logging hooks to the installer to emit backoff/retry metrics and counts for mount failures to aid quantification. (Owner: Jordan).

Retro notes / lessons learned: 
- Onprem installs frequently encounter network middleboxes with stateful heuristics that don't fail obvious — need a standard checklist to detect conntrack pressure early.
- Our default NFS mounting behavior at scale creates many short TCP sessions; exploring a long-lived connection strategy or NFS client caching may reduce load.
- Tight coupling of overlay + small MTU environments must be flagged in pre-install network prep (we should detect and warn about <1500 MTU network on the preflight script).

Next standup (tentative): 2024-10-15 10:00 PDT — focus on mitigation progress, PR reviews, and customer vendor ticket status.

Notes to self: keep the repro harness sanitized before sharing with vendor (remove customer IPs), tag PCAPs with timestamps, and ensure we rotate any sensitive keys before uploading artifacts to shared drive.

Appendix — quick command snippets used in debugging: 
- Show conntrack counters: sudo cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count && sudo sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max
- MSS clamp example: iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
- Temporary mount tweak: mount -o nconnect=4,actimeo=1,nfsvers=4.1 server:/export /mnt/pv

End of notes.
